# BlueTeam.News
### Threat Landscape Briefing · 2026-09-06 · Sunday

## BLUF
Nine CVEs now confirmed on CISA's KEV catalog this week — spanning Chrome, SonicWall SMA1000, PaperCut, JFrog Artifactory, and Sangoma Switchvox — meaning any organization with exposed edge appliances or unpatched browsers faces multiple live exploitation paths simultaneously, not a single incident.

---

## EXECUTIVE SUMMARY — SHIFT DECISIONS

- **Threat:** Nine separate CVEs added to CISA KEV in the past five days (CVE-2026-85046 Chrome, CVE-2026-83548/83549 SonicWall SMA1000, CVE-2026-81578/82078 PaperCut, CVE-2026-82329 JFrog Artifactory, CVE-2026-9586 Sangoma Switchvox, CVE-2026-48710 Starlette, CVE-2026-49869 Kestra, CVE-2026-59822 LiteLLM), all with confirmed active exploitation.

- **Exposure:** Declared watch topics (Fortinet, Ivanti, Citrix) show no matches this cycle; verify whether SonicWall SMA1000, Chrome, PaperCut, JFrog Artifactory, or Sangoma Switchvox are present in inventory — none are confirmed in this organization's stack from current evidence.

- **Required decisions:** Infrastructure — force-verify Chrome version ≥152.0.7977.82 across managed endpoints, CVE-2026-85046 — recommended target September 8, 2026; Infrastructure — if SMA1000 is deployed, apply hotfix 12.4.3-03526 or 12.5.0-02952 and treat as potentially pre-compromised, CVE-2026-83548/CVE-2026-83549 — recommended target September 8, 2026; Infrastructure — if PaperCut MF/NG deployed, apply Emergency Patch Release 2 immediately, CVE-2026-81578/CVE-2026-82078 — recommended target September 8, 2026.

---

## KEY JUDGMENTS

### Signal 1 — [Horizon 1] Chrome zero-day exploited, patch rollout still incomplete
**Assessment:** Google confirms active in-the-wild exploitation of a V8 type confusion flaw that can trigger remote code execution via crafted web content, and the fix is still rolling out — meaning unpatched endpoints remain exposed today.

**Confidence:** High — Google's own advisory and CISA KEV addition confirm exploitation; CVSS and version details corroborated by CCCS, Help Net Security, The Hacker News, and BleepingComputer.

**What happened:** CVE-2026-85046, CVSS 8.8 [The Hacker News, 2026-09-04](https://thehackernews.com/2026/09/google-releases-chrome-update-to-patch.html), fixed in Chrome 152.0.7977.82/.83 (Windows/macOS) and 152.0.7977.82 (Linux). CISA added CVE-2026-85046 to KEV on 2026-09-04; FCEB remediation for CVE-2026-85046 is due 2026-09-18 per the captured catalog record. This is the sixth actively exploited Chrome zero-day patched in 2026 [BleepingComputer, 2026-09-04](https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/google-warns-of-new-chrome-zero-day-flaw-exploited-in-attacks/); [CISA Advisories, 2026-09-04](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2026/09/04/cisa-adds-one-known-exploited-vulnerability-catalog).

**Defender impact:** Browser fleet management and endpoint patch compliance are the control at stake — check auto-update status on managed Chrome installs; rollout is gradual, so version-check enforcement (not just push timing) determines actual exposure window.

**Recommended actions:**
- **Act now:** Infrastructure — force-verify Chrome version ≥152.0.7977.82 across managed endpoints, CVE-2026-85046 — recommended target September 8, 2026.
- Detection engineering — monitor for anomalous renderer-process crashes/behavior consistent with V8 type confusion exploitation — recommended target September 12, 2026.

**Decision window:** Current shift

**The line:** Google's sixth exploited Chrome zero-day this year is patched, but until every browser reports the new build number we have unpatched attack surface open right now.

---

### Signal 2 — [Horizon 1] SonicWall SMA1000 zero-day chain enables pre-auth RCE
**Assessment:** SonicWall confirms active exploitation of a chainable SSRF-plus-command-injection pair in SMA1000 edge appliances, and separate reporting notes this is one of several SMA1000 vulnerabilities exploited since late 2025 — a single vendor's count, not an industry-wide ranking.

**Confidence:** High — vendor confirmed exploitation directly; Rapid7 and CCCS corroborate technical chain mechanics and KEV status.

**What happened:** CVE-2026-83548 (CVSS 10.0, pre-auth SSRF) [Rapid7, 2026-09-02](https://www.rapid7.com/blog/post/etr-critical-sonicwall-sma1000-vulnerabilities-cve-2026-83548-cve-2026-83549-exploited-in-the-wild) and CVE-2026-83549 (OS command injection, no CVSS supported in retained passages for this record) affect SMA1000 models 6210/7210/8200v on versions 12.4.3-03453 and 12.5.0-02835 platform-hotfix and earlier. CISA added both to KEV on 2026-09-02; FCEB remediation for CVE-2026-83548 and CVE-2026-83549 is due 2026-09-05 per the captured catalog record — that federal deadline has passed. Fixed in 12.4.3-03526 / 12.5.0-02952 [The Hacker News, 2026-09-02](https://thehackernews.com/2026/09/attackers-exploit-two-sonicwall-sma.html); [CISA Advisories, 2026-09-02](https://www.cisa.gov/news-events/alerts/2026/09/02/cisa-adds-seven-known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog). CyberScoop separately notes SonicWall SMA 1000 appliances have had five actively exploited vulnerabilities since late 2025, a count specific to that reporting, not a comparative ranking against other vendors [CyberScoop, 2026-09-03](https://cyberscoop.com/sonicwall-sma1000-zero-days-actively-exploited/).

**Relevance:** SonicWall is a declared watch-adjacent edge-appliance vendor category alongside Fortinet/Citrix/Ivanti interests; local SMA1000 deployment status is unknown and must be verified, not assumed absent.

**Defender impact:** Exploitation reportedly predates disclosure — patching alone does not confirm a clean appliance. Prioritize log review of Work Place interface and AMC access before applying hotfixes.

**Recommended actions:**
- **Act now:** Infrastructure — if SMA1000 is deployed, apply hotfix 12.4.3-03526 or 12.5.0-02952 and treat as potentially pre-compromised, CVE-2026-83548/CVE-2026-83549 — recommended target September 8, 2026.
- Incident response — review appliance logs for pre-patch admin/API access; re-image if compromise indicators found — recommended target September 10, 2026.

**Decision window:** Current shift

**The line:** SonicWall confirms these two flaws were exploited before disclosure, and the federal fix deadline has already passed, so patching alone won't tell us whether an exposed appliance was already compromised.

---

### Signal 3 — [Horizon 1] PaperCut flaws now used for credential theft in education
**Assessment:** Exploitation of PaperCut MF/NG has moved from generic RCE risk to a targeted credential-harvesting campaign against US and European schools and universities, per Arctic Wolf observation.

**Confidence:** Moderate — Arctic Wolf-sourced reporting via The Hacker News establishes sector targeting and technique; underlying article retrieval was partial (opening excluded as unusable), limiting full campaign detail.

**What happened:** CVE-2026-81578 (CVSS 9.8) [NVD, date unavailable](https://services.nvd.nist.gov/rest/json/cves/2.0?cveId=CVE-2026-81578) and CVE-2026-82078 (authentication bypass + RCE chain, no CVSS supported in retained passages) affect PaperCut MF/NG prior to v24/25/26 Emergency Patch Release 2. CISA added both to KEV on 2026-08-31; FCEB remediation for CVE-2026-81578 and CVE-2026-82078 is due 2026-09-14 per the captured catalog record [The Hacker News, 2026-09-05](https://thehackernews.com/2026/09/attackers-exploit-papercut-flaws-to.html); [CCCS, 2026-08-31](https://cyber.gc.ca/en/alerts-advisories/papercut-security-advisory-av26-858).

**Defender impact:** Print management servers are a soft target for lateral credential harvesting — check PaperCut server logs for reconnaissance/command execution and verify Emergency Patch Release 2 is applied on any instance.

**Recommended actions:**
- Infrastructure — if PaperCut MF/NG deployed, apply Emergency Patch Release 2 immediately, CVE-2026-81578/CVE-2026-82078 — recommended target September 8, 2026.
- Detection engineering — hunt for anomalous command execution/credential access on print servers per Arctic Wolf indicators — recommended target September 12, 2026.

**Decision window:** 72 hours

**The line:** Attackers are now using PaperCut access specifically to steal credentials from schools, so any exposed print server is a stepping stone into the broader network.

---

### Signal 4 — [Horizon 1] JFrog Artifactory auth-bypass exploited within days of disclosure
**Assessment:** An authentication bypass in Artifactory granting admin-level access was weaponized by attackers "merely days" after public disclosure, per watchTowr research, underscoring compressed exploit timelines for CI/CD infrastructure.

**Confidence:** High — three independent publishers (Dark Reading, The Hacker News, CCCS) plus KEV confirmation corroborate exploitation and mechanism; exact hours-to-exploit interval is not stated in retained sources.

**What happened:** CVE-2026-82329, CVSS 9.8 [NVD, date unavailable](https://services.nvd.nist.gov/rest/json/cves/2.0?cveId=CVE-2026-82329), allows admin token minting under default configuration in Artifactory versions prior to 7.111.21/7.117.28/7.125.20/7.133.29/7.146.38/7.161.20. CISA added CVE-2026-82329 to KEV on 2026-09-02; FCEB remediation for CVE-2026-82329 is due 2026-09-05 per the captured catalog record — that federal deadline has passed [The Hacker News, 2026-09-01](https://thehackernews.com/2026/09/attackers-exploit-critical-jfrog.html); [Dark Reading, 2026-09-01](https://www.darkreading.com/application-security/attackers-pounce-critical-artifactory-flaw-disclosure); [CCCS, 2026-09-02](https://cyber.gc.ca/en/alerts-advisories/jfrog-security-advisory-av26-867).

**Defender impact:** CI/CD artifact repositories are a supply-chain pivot point — verify Artifactory version and audit for unexpected admin tokens minted since late August.

**Recommended actions:**
- Application security — if Artifactory deployed, upgrade to patched release and audit all admin tokens issued since 2026-08-28, CVE-2026-82329 — recommended target September 9, 2026.

**Decision window:** 72 hours

**The line:** A CI/CD repository flaw went from disclosure to active admin-token abuse in days, which is now a passed federal remediation deadline for anyone still exposed.

---

### Signal 5 — [Horizon 2] Sangoma Switchvox SQLi joins a pattern of rapid appliance exploitation
**Assessment:** An unauthenticated SQL injection in enterprise VoIP platform Switchvox grants remote code execution and was weaponized with public IOCs within a day of disclosure, adding another confirmed edge-facing appliance to this week's exploitation wave.

**Confidence:** High — Horizon3 exploitation warning, CISA KEV addition, and NVD scoring corroborate; SecurityWeek and The Hacker News align on mechanism. Note the vendor-cited score and NVD score differ: vendor advisory reports 9.3, NVD lists 9.8 for the same CVE.

**What happened:** CVE-2026-9586 — vendor advisory cites CVSS 9.3 [SecurityWeek, 2026-09-04](https://www.securityweek.com/sangoma-switchvox-vulnerabilities-exploited-in-the-wild/); NVD lists CVSS 9.8 [NVD, date unavailable](https://services.nvd.nist.gov/rest/json/cves/2.0?cveId=CVE-2026-9586) — is unauthenticated SQLi via unsanitized PhoneIP parameter in Switchvox SMB Edition 8.3 (104997), enabling arbitrary PostgreSQL commands and RCE. CISA added CVE-2026-9586 to KEV on 2026-09-02; FCEB remediation for CVE-2026-9586 is due 2026-09-05 per the captured catalog record — that federal deadline has passed [The Hacker News, 2026-09-02](https://thehackernews.com/2026/09/attackers-exploit-critical-switchvox.html).

**Defender impact:** VoIP management systems often sit on internal networks with database access — verify Switchvox exposure to the internet and confirm patch status.

**Recommended actions:**
- **Act now:** Infrastructure — if Switchvox SMB Edition deployed, isolate from internet exposure and apply vendor patch, CVE-2026-9586 — recommended target September 8, 2026.
- Detection engineering — deploy Horizon3-published IOCs for CVE-2026-9586 exploitation detection — recommended target September 9, 2026.

**Decision window:** Current shift

**The line:** A single crafted request against an exposed VoIP appliance can now yield full database and system control, and the federal remediation deadline for this flaw has already passed.

---

### Signal 6 — [Horizon 2] Patch volume climbing while confirmed exploitation stays narrow
**Assessment:** Vendors are shipping record patch volumes (August 2026 was the second-largest Patch Tuesday in history) while only a small fraction of disclosed CVEs see confirmed exploitation, sharpening the case for prioritization over patch-everything cadence.

**Confidence:** Moderate — Help Net Security's own aggregation states counts directly; this is a single publisher's editorial forecast, not independently verified vendor data.

**What happened:** August 2026 Patch Tuesday resolved 398 CVEs (42 Critical, 355 Important, 1 Moderate); only one was confirmed actively exploited, two disclosed pre-patch [Help Net Security, 2026-09-04](https://www.helpnetsecurity.com/2026/09/04/september-2026-patch-tuesday-forecast/).

**Defender impact:** Vulnerability management should weight KEV membership and exploitation evidence over raw CVE/CVSS count when triaging September patch cycles.

**Recommended actions:**
- Detection engineering — align September patch triage priority to KEV-listed CVEs first, general Critical-rated patches second — recommended target September 15, 2026.

**Decision window:** 30 days

**The line:** Patch volume keeps climbing, but confirmed active exploitation stays rare — so we patch by evidence of exploitation, not by CVSS score alone.

---

## DEVELOPING SITUATIONS

### CrowdStrike Falcon privilege-escalation exploit now public
**Trajectory:** Unchanged from prior briefing — a public PoC ("FalconFlank") for a Falcon sensor privilege-escalation flaw was reported by BleepingComputer and The Register; no new exploitation-in-the-wild evidence today, still PoC-stage.

**Watch criteria:** Escalate when CrowdStrike issues a patch advisory, a CVE is assigned, or exploitation in the wild is confirmed.

### AI-generated ransomware operation reporting (The Register)
**Trajectory:** Uncertain — a title-only/limited passage claims AI agents executed a full ransomware attack chain; no technical detail retained to confirm mechanics, victim, or scale.

**Watch criteria:** Escalate when a substantive technical writeup or vendor confirmation names the actor, victim, or malware family involved.

### Magento/Adobe Commerce "StyleSmuggler" zero-day
**Trajectory:** New — Sansec reports an unpatched authentication-free RCE in Magento Open Source/Adobe Commerce actively exploited since September 4, 2026; no vendor patch confirmed in retained evidence.

**Watch criteria:** Escalate when Adobe issues a patch or CVE assignment, or when CISA adds it to KEV.

---

## CONVERGENCE

### Edge-appliance exploitation cadence outpaces patch-cycle assumptions
**The intersection:** Both the SonicWall SMA1000 chain and the JFrog Artifactory bypass show attackers weaponizing disclosed vulnerabilities in internet-facing infrastructure within a very short window — SonicWall confirmed exploitation predated public disclosure, and Artifactory was exploited "merely days" after disclosure [Rapid7, 2026-09-02](https://www.rapid7.com/blog/post/etr-critical-sonicwall-sma1000-vulnerabilities-cve-2026-83548-cve-2026-83549-exploited-in-the-wild); [The Hacker News, 2026-09-01](https://thehackernews.com/2026/09/attackers-exploit-critical-jfrog.html). The shared mechanism is that standard patch-cycle assumptions (patch within a week of disclosure) no longer outrun exploitation for edge-facing appliances and CI/CD infrastructure.

**The cascade:** If disclosure-to-exploitation windows keep compressing for both network-edge and DevOps-adjacent products, standard weekly patch cadence could leave a compromise window open even for teams meeting normal SLAs — this is a hypothesis based on two cited cases, not an established population trend.

**The move:** Prepare — build a compressed-SLA patch track (48–72 hours) specifically for internet-facing appliances and CI/CD infrastructure with KEV-listed CVEs.

**Confirmation:** Check whether future KEV additions in this category continue to show pre-disclosure or days-post-disclosure exploitation timing; monitor CISA KEV catalog additions weekly.

**Action rationale:** A compressed-SLA track shortens the exposure window itself, unlike a standard monthly patch cadence, which the cascade above notes will fail against exploitation occurring within days of disclosure.

---

## WATCHLIST — THROUGH 2026-09-09

- CISA adds another CVE to the KEV catalog before September 9, 2026.
- CrowdStrike issues a patch advisory or CVE for the FalconFlank privilege-escalation exploit.
- Adobe/Magento releases a patch or CVE for the StyleSmuggler zero-day.
- SonicWall confirms a third SMA1000 vulnerability under active exploitation.
- Arctic Wolf or another vendor publishes IOCs for the PaperCut education-sector credential-theft campaign.
- A named ransomware group is confirmed to have used autonomous AI agents in a documented attack (resolving the Register's limited report).
- FBI or Louisiana identity-verification company issues a statement on the 153-million driver's license breach.

sources.evidenceText: CISA Adds One Known Exploited Vulnerability to Catalog Alert CISA Adds One Known Exploited Vulnerability to Catalog Release Date September 04, 2026 CISA has added one new vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog , based on evidence of active exploitation. CVE-2026-85046 Google Chromium V8 Type Confusion Vulnerability This type of vulnerability is a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and poses significant risks to the federal enterprise. Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04: Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk establishes vulnerability management requirements for Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies. BOD 26-04 reinforces the importance of the KEV Catalog and requires federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities, specifically those identified by Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) listed in CISA’s KEV Catalog on publicly exposed assets that grant total control of the asset post-exploitation, while deferring action for lower-risk vulnerabilities. BOD 26-04 further establishes basic expectations for when agencies must check whether threat actors compromised the system before the patch was applied. While BOD 26-04 applies only to FCEB agencies, CISA encourages all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management and prioritize remediation of KEV Catalog vulnerabilities . CISA will continue to add vulnerabilities to the catalog that meet the specified criteria . Aware of an exploited vulnerability not currently listed in the KEV Catalog? Submit it for potential addition through CISA’s KEV Nomination Form . Potential KEV additions must have a CVE ID, evidence of exploitation, and clear mitigation guidance. sources.evidenceText: Sangoma Switchvox Vulnerabilities Exploited in the Wild Threat actors have been exploiting a critical-severity vulnerability in the enterprise VoIP telephony management solution Sangoma Switchvox, Horizon3 and CISA warn. Tracked as CVE-2026-9586 (CVSS score of 9.3) and described as an unauthenticated SQL injection issue, the security defect can be exploited remotely for arbitrary code execution. It resides in an endpoint that processes XML content, which did not perform sanitization or parameterization when concatenating the user-controlled PhoneIP value into PostgreSQL queries. “An unauthenticated remote attacker can execute arbitrary SQL statements against the backend PostgreSQL database using a single crafted request, including database operations and remote code execution,” a NIST advisory reads. On Tuesday, cybersecurity firm Horizon3 warned that threat actors had started exploiting CVE-2026-9586 in the wild and shared indicators of compromise (IoCs) to help organizations identify potential intrusions. On Wednesday, the US cybersecurity agency CISA added the security flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities ( KEV ) catalog along with six other issues, including the JFrog Artifactory bug and two SonicWall SMA1000 zero-days recently flagged as exploited. sources.evidenceText: CISA Adds Seven Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog CISA has added seven new vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog, based on evidence of active exploitation. Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04: Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk establishes vulnerability management requirements for Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies. BOD 26-04 reinforces the importance of the KEV Catalog and requires federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities, specifically those identified by Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) listed in CISA’s KEV Catalog on publicly exposed assets that grant total control of the asset post-exploitation, while deferring action for lower-risk vulnerabilities. BOD 26-04 further establishes basic expectations for when agencies must check whether threat actors compromised the system before the patch was applied. While BOD 26-04 applies only to FCEB agencies, CISA encourages all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management and prioritize remediation of KEV Catalog vulnerabilities. CISA will continue to add vulnerabilities to the catalog that meet the specified criteria. Aware of an exploited vulnerability not currently listed in the KEV Catalog? The vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-83548 and CVE-2026-83549, can be chained to achieve unauthenticated remote code execution (RCE) on affected appliances. CVE-2026-83548 is a critical pre-authentication server-side request forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in the SMA1000 Appliance Work Place interface. The flaw has a CVSS v3.1 base score of 10.0 and can allow a remote, unauthenticated attacker to access sensitive functionality and perform unauthorized operations through an unintended alternate access path. CVE-2026-83549 is a high-severity OS command injection vulnerability in the Appliance Management Console (AMC). On its own, exploitation requires an authenticated administrator and specific system conditions. Although, by leveraging the SSRF vulnerability CVE-2026-83548 an attacker could potentially exploit CVE-2026-83549 to execute arbitrary OS commands without prior authentication. SonicWall SMA1000 appliances are enterprise secure remote access gateways used to provide employees and other authorized users with access to internal applications and resources. Their role as network-edge systems makes successful exploitation particularly concerning, since affected Work Place interfaces may be exposed directly to the internet as part of normal deployment. SonicWall has confirmed active exploitation of both vulnerabilities in the wild, and both CVE-2026-83548 and CVE-2026-83549 have been added to CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities ( KEV ) catalog. sources.title: DPRK APTs: Ted backdoor and curlRAT target South Korean media and automotive sectors
sources.evidenceText: DPRK APTs: Ted backdoor and curlRAT target South Korean media and automotive sectors Overview A new Linux toolkit, identified by Rapid7 Labs, has been targeting organizations across South Korea’s automotive and media industries with minimal detection. The campaign made use of a HAProxy instance named “ted backdoor”, alongside trojanized versions of crond, agetty, atd, sshd, and polkitd. This previously undocumented framework enabled threat actors to execute remote commands on compromised servers, inject malicious scripts into web traffic, perform credential harvesting, and engage in long-term surveillance. The standout feature of this toolkit is its depth of integration with the target environment. The ted backdoor is compiled as part of the victim’s existing HAProxy version 2.8.12. It uses its native filter API, internal memory pools, event scheduler, and process management infrastructure to intercept traffic and hide from monitoring, while genuine load balancing traffic operates as expected. Operating alongside this are an SSH keylogger, a curl-based RAT, and a stager. The RAT maintains a watchdog thread dedicated to tracking HAProxy’s health, and reporting it back to the operator’s infrastructure. The earliest uploads on VirusTotal date back to mid-2025 and the involved HAProxy 2.8.12-0fdb194 was released on 22 November 2024, establishing this as the earliest possible compilation date for this build. The toolkit is attributed with medium confidence to DPRK APTs, given that the attacks Rapid7 observed were targeting South Korean media and automotive sectors, likely aiming at long-term espionage, the usage of simple xor-based encryption, custom substitution cipher, and the list of C2s hardcoded is associated to APT37 by ThreatFox and maltrail. Analysis shows that the ted backdoor could be part of a broader framework covering nginx backdoor as well. The ted plugin registers a custom HAProxy filter that hooks the HTTP parser to inspect and log high-value traffic, steal session cookies, and perform a client IP selection to decide whether to inject custom scripts in the webpage being rendered. Technical analysis Rapid7 researchers revealed that the toolkit was used in campaigns targeting South Korean automotive and media sectors likely dating back to early 2025. The number of trojanized binaries and functionalities found suggest the scope could be long-term cyber espionage and surveillance. However, gathered evidence does not suffice to establish a timeline nor how the initial access was performed. At the time of analysis, both victims were running an edge webserver with ports 80, 443, and 25 exposed. Port 443 hosted the Groupware login portal and port 25 exposed a mail server. Either surface represents a plausible initial access vector consistent with documented Kimsuky tradecraft. Since the beginning of 2026 Kimsuky has been observed exploiting RCE vulnerabilities in externally accessible mail servers to compromise South Korean groupware vendors, while Groupware web portals represent the kind of exposed authenticated application that DPRK-nexus actors have repeatedly targeted for credential harvesting and exploitation. The specific entry point and any associated CVE remain unconfirmed pending further forensic evidence. The scenario shown in Figure 1 assumes the initial access is obtained by exploitation of CVEs related to the Groupware portal. Figure 1: Attack chain partially reconstructed ⠀ The threat actor begins by exploiting a vulnerability in the Groupware login portal running on the edge webserver, gaining an initial foothold in the DMZ. From there, they establish persistence and harvest credentials from the compromised edge host (e.g. SSH keylogger), which also doubles as a staging server hosting the trojanized system ELFs. With a foothold on the edge, the attacker pivots inward and drops the stager onto internal servers. The stager checks for the presence of either crond or HAProxy, and only then deploys CurlRAT retrieving it either from its data section or the edge webserver. In parallel, ted backdoor is dropped onto the HAProxy load balancer. Once active,it establishes its own C2 channel to the external operator infrastructure, enabling data exfiltration, command execution, and script injection. On the victim side, the compromised load balancer silently redirects or serves malicious content to selected clients browsing through it, completing the watering-hole loop. SSH keylogger 4bb923eb040aa13ca8fd409c31ee4729c60ddff32e350efe1c5a4a9168a065f5 intercepts legitimate users' plaintext passwords and saves them to an encrypted log file under /var/lib/sshd/c8c68e629bba773a10ac80012d10bf19.

sources.evidenceText: Financially Motivated Threat Actor BREEZE COMET Targets Brazil Introduction Beginning in 2024 Mandiant investigated a string of compromises affecting Brazilian financial services, retail, and eCommerce organizations. Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) tracks this activity as BREEZE COMET (formerly UNC5669), a financially motivated threat actor specializing in manipulating payment systems and banking software in Brazil to conduct fraudulent transfers. This activity overlaps with operations publicly reported as Plump Spider and SHADOW-AETHER-064. In this blog, we detail BREEZE COMET’s tactics and toolkit, and provide mitigation recommendations and detections to support organizations in defending against this active and developing threat. BREEZE COMET tactics have evolved over time to leverage a customized malware suite and compromised, trusted websites to facilitate initial access, command and control (C2), and to interact with financial software and payment APIs. BREEZE COMET’s operational infrastructure may also indicate intent to expand their infrastructure footprint to other countries in Latin America and Africa. Additionally, we have evidence that BREEZE COMET is using generative artificial intelligence (AI) to support malware development, which may further increase the scale, speed, and sophistication of their operations in the future. BREEZE COMET Targets Brazilian Financial Technology BREEZE COMET operations target organizations with permission to conduct transactions through banking software, APIs, and payment systems such as Pix, STR, and Boleto. This typically includes banks, payment processors, retailers, exchanges, as well as fintech and banking software providers. To achieve their objective of conducting fraudulent transfers, BREEZE COMET must maintain: Access to the National Financial System Network (Rede Nacional do Setor Financeiro, RSFN) through an entity with this access. Access to mTLS credentials that allow sending authenticated payloads with transactional orders to Pix, STR (Brazilian Reserves Transfer System), or any transactional listener to be executed with minimal restrictions in the name of an organization with available funds. Persistent access to multiple accounts in targeted organizations’ Active Directory and/or cloud environments. Understanding of an organization’s transfer processing procedures, network controls, fintech integrations and anti-fraud systems. In order to support these requirements, BREEZE COMET evolved to operate in multiple compromised environments at the same time, crafting custom C2 malware to automate activities such as reconnaissance, lateral movement, persistence, and exfiltration. Initial Compromise and Establish Foothold BREEZE COMET has used various methods for initial access. In early compromises, Mandiant observed this threat actor use password spraying as well as voice calls impersonating IT support teams to convince users to install Remote Monitoring and Management (RMM) tools such as AnyDesk. Axur corroborates use of voice phishing, and suggests that the group has also attempted to recruit insiders at targeted organizations. In mid-2025, GTIG observed BREEZE COMET using compromised Brazilian small government websites to stage RMM tools, infostealers disguised as legitimate tax or receipt documents (e.g., ComprovantePDF.exe ), or backdoors such as XWORM set to persist via automated startup shortcut modifications. XWORM is a backdoor that is widely available for purchase on cyber crime forums, with leaked or “cracked” versions also available. BREEZE COMET then used these compromised government websites to facilitate social engineering operations for initial access, and as C2 endpoints. The use of compromised, trusted infrastructure allowed the threat actors to avoid detection by network domain reputation filters. GTIG also observed BREEZE COMET replicating this behavior with municipal domains in Nigeria, Paraguay, Ghana, and Venezuela, suggesting a potentially growing targeting focus. Analysis of compromised municipal domains indicated that BREEZE COMET reused the same staging infrastructure to host and deliver XWORM payloads across operations targeting multiple organizations.
